subject: Brightline trial: success criteria, prompt/log handoff & delivery plan
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Ellie Barnes <ellie@brightline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Jul 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Brightline trial: success criteria, prompt/log handoff & delivery plan

Hi Ellie — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have shared expectations for the trial: 

1) Trial goal (what success looks like)
- Achieve >= 92% intent-classification accuracy on your production prompt-set (sampled) AND median 95th-percentile generation latency <= 300ms for 256-token responses under a 1-client concurrency profile.
- Team sign-off metric: CSAT >= 4/5 from 10 qualitative reviewers on representative outputs.

2) What we need from Brightline by EOD Friday (2028-07-08) to hit the timeline:
- Prompt/log bundle: compressed CSV (prompt_id, user_prompt, context, expected_response, metadata) — sample 1,500 prompts across Support/Docs/Search flows. Prefer UTF-8, comma-delimited. 
- Redaction guidance: indicate which fields contain PII and provide a sample redaction map.
- Baseline outputs: 200 human-labeled pairs (prompt -> expected response) for evaluation.

3) Redwood deliverables and owners
- Eval plan & scoring rubric (Marissa) — will provide thresholded metrics and per-prompt failure classification.
- Inference runbook + instance config we’ll use for the trial (Karthik) — includes batching and cache settings to meet latency targets.
- Weekly touchpoint cadence and demo schedule for results review (Jordan)

4) Timeline (proposed)
- July 8: Brightline uploads prompt/log bundle to the shared Drive folder + confirms redaction map.
- July 10–12: Redwood runs ingest + initial eval pass; shares interim results and failure examples.
- July 15: Joint review call to validate metrics and discuss any prompt re-sampling.

5) Security & procurement notes
- If procurement requires a formal SOW or an NDA addendum before data upload, loop them in and copy procurement@brightline.ai.

Attachments: POC_Success_Criteria_v1.xlsx (outline), brightline_prompt_template.csv (template)

Next step: Ellie — can you confirm ability to deliver the 1,500 prompt sample and redaction map by EOD Friday? If there's procurement gating, let us know and we’ll shift accordingly.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

--

From: Ellie Barnes <ellie@brightline.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@brightline.ai>
Date: Thu, 6 Jul 2028 09:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Brightline trial: success criteria, prompt/log handoff & delivery plan

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the clear summary. Quick answers from our side: 

- We can provide the 1,500-sample bundle, but need to confirm two items on your CSV spec: we have nested JSON in our metadata column (session context). Would Redwood prefer that field flattened into a string or a separate JSON file per prompt?
- Redaction: we can provide a redaction map. We’ll need a short template from you for PII masking examples.
- Procurement: we generally need an MSA amendment for any data exchange over S3. I’ve CC’d procurement; they’ll advise if they need a one-off addendum.

We can target uploading the bundle by EOD Friday if procurement doesn't block the S3 share. If procurement requires an on-prem transfer instead, we’ll need a day or two more.

Ellie
Head of Product, Brightline AI
ellie@brightline.ai

On Wed, Jul 5, 2028 at 2:12 PM Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Ellie — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have shared expectations for the trial:
> ...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ellie Barnes <ellie@brightline.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Jul 2028 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightline trial: success criteria, prompt/log handoff & delivery plan

Hey team — jumping in with the evaluation plan and clarifications on the deliverables. High-level:

- Eval artifacts we’ll produce: per-prompt pass/fail, intent confusion matrix, response-quality notes (scored 1–5), latency distribution, and a digest of top 25 failure examples with suggested prompt fixes.
- For the metadata/json column: we can accept a single-column JSON string (UTF-8). Please ensure newlines are escaped. If you can also include a small sample (first 200 rows) as plain CSV, that speeds triage.
- Redaction template: I attached a short example redaction map (redaction_example.json) and a one-page checklist for secure upload. I’ll put both into the Drive folder Jordan linked.

Ownership:
- Marissa: Evaluation rubric, labeling instructions for the 200 human-labeled anchors.
- Karthik: Testbed config and inference tuning; will recommend quantization and batching settings for the trial.
- Sean: Observability/trace hooks and token-level cost estimates.

If Brightline can upload the sample by the 8th, we’ll aim to produce an initial results deck by the 12th. If procurement introduces a >48 hour gating delay, please flag and we'll reprioritize the ingest order (start with a 200-row sample first).

Attachments referenced: redaction_example.json (text), POC_Labeling_Guidelines.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Lead, Evaluation & Evals Ops | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellie Barnes <ellie@brightline.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Jul 2028 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightline trial: success criteria, prompt/log handoff & delivery plan

Quick technical notes from infra/serving side:

- File format: CSV is fine with the metadata column as escaped JSON. If upload to S3, please gzip the CSV to reduce transfer time.
- Required fields: prompt_id, user_prompt, context (optional), expected_response (if available), source_label, timestamp. If any field is missing at upload, include an empty column rather than dropping the column.
- We'll provision a dedicated GPU pool for the trial (n1-standard equivalent), and test both 8-bit and FP16 variants to hit the latency target. I’ll publish the exact instance config to the Drive folder by EOD today.
- Data access: we prefer S3 presigned URLs for ingestion. If procurement blocks S3, we can accept secure upload to a Redwoods-managed SFTP endpoint (details in Drive).

I’ll also add a short checklist for sample size prioritization (if you can only share a subset initially).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Infrastructure Lead, Dedicated & Private | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Ellie Barnes <ellie@brightline.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@brightline.ai>
Date: Fri, 7 Jul 2028 16:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Brightline trial: success criteria, prompt/log handoff & delivery plan

Thanks everyone — procurement confirmed the S3 share is OK under our existing MSA; they’ll provide the bucket and role by Monday morning. We’ll plan to: 

- Upload gzip CSV to the shared bucket by EOD Monday (2028-07-10). It will include the metadata JSON as an escaped field and the 200-row labeled anchors inline.
- We reviewed the evaluation rubric and are comfortable with the proposed pass/fail thresholds; we’ll reserve a small ad-hoc re-sample if you find the initial sample noisy.

Jordan — let’s keep the July 15 call on the calendar. Thanks for the clear owners — look forward to the initial results.

Ellie

Attachments: none
